comment: The models the generator can run, each pinned by revision and by the sha256 of its weights, with its licence. `default` is what `make artgen` uses; MODEL=<name> picks another. Every committed example records the model that made it.
default_comment: Chosen on 2026-10-14 by the owner, after the same seven prompts on both: Z-Image-Turbo drew cleaner, flatter pixel art that reads at 32 pixels; klein drew more detailed, illustrated pictures. See ADR 0013.

zimage.settings_comment: The model card's: 9 steps (8 forward passes), guidance 0 -- the Turbo model uses no guidance and no negative prompt.
zimage.fp8_comment: Measured: its transformer is about 12.3 GB in bfloat16, over a 12 GB card on its own, and model offload ran out of memory. Stored in 8-bit floats and computed in bfloat16 it peaked at 8.3 GB, 13 s a picture. Group offload with streams instead sat at 0% GPU for seven minutes and was stopped.
zimage.licence_comment: The repository has no LICENSE file at this revision; the licence is the model card's metadata, read through the Hugging Face API on 2026-10-14.

lora.scale_comment: Measured, not taken from the card. The LoRA is rsLoRA (rank 64, alpha 128), which diffusers scales by alpha/sqrt(rank) = 16; the card's 'strength 0.85-1.4' is ComfyUI's, which scales by alpha/rank = 2. At 1.0 here the output was black noise, at 0.25 a blur, at 0.125 -- 2/16, the card's 1.0 -- a clean sprite.
lora.training_data_comment: The card says its training images are CC0, and gives two sizes for that dataset (500 and 1,010). A claim, not checked.

klein-walk.purpose_comment: Walking sheets only (T33): manifest entries of kind `walk` name it, and nothing else uses it. The base model, not the distilled `klein`: the LoRA card says the distilled one 'ruins the quality of the pixels and the consistency'.
klein-walk.text_encoder_comment: The base model's text encoder is byte for byte the distilled model's -- the same sha256 in both repositories' listings, measured in T31 and again in T33's review -- so it is taken from `klein`'s repository, the encoder's files only, rather than fetched under a second name.
klein-walk.settings_comment: The LoRA card's: 512 pixels, the size of the sheets it was trained on; the base model's 50 steps and guidance 4. Measured on 2026-10-14, nine sheets between T31 and T33: 23-57 s a sheet, the first of a run the slowest, 8.3 GB peak, with model offload.

lora.weights_comment: The 3000-step file, which the card says is the more consistent with figures; the other is its 2750-step checkpoint.
lora.scale_comment: Unscaled, as T31 measured it: the sheet the owner judged good enough was made at the adapter's default.
lora.training_data_comment: The card credits its training sheets to a template by George Bailey, CC BY 4.0 (https://opengameart.org/content/16x16-game-assets). Whether a sheet made with it owes that attribution is not settled here, so no sheet it makes is committed: they stay in the gitignored folder, a person's own.

klein-walk.kinds_comment: It makes only walking sheets: given a still sprite's prompt, the LoRA still draws a 4 by 4 sheet. The generator refuses any other kind.
